Job lived in Jacob's time and married Dinah.

translationCredits.attribution:
Divrei Shalom v'Emet, tanslated by M. Bohnen, 2020 · https://www.sefaria.org/ · When Joseph Klausner wrote his survey of modern Hebrew literature, he began with Divrei Shalom v’Emet, (Words of Peace and Truth) written by Naftali Herz Wessely in 1782. Salo Baron called it the “first manifesto of Haskalah.” It was attacked by the Rabbis, and some even burned copies of the letter in public.
The letter was written in response to an Edict of Tolerance issued on January 2, 1782 by Emperor Joseph II of Austria. The Emperor’s goal was “to make the Jewish people useful to the State.” Among other things, the Edict allowed Jews to attend public schools and universities or open their own schools if they operated like the public schools. While many in the Jewish community were skeptical, the Edict found an enthusiastic promoter in Wessely, a poet, linguist and biblical commentator. He composed a letter in Hebrew to the Jewish community urging them to establish schools where secular subjects would be taught in addition to the study of Jewish texts.
While portions of the letter have been translated into English, this is the first English translation of the entire letter. This translation is based on דברי שלום ואמת, published by Anton Schmid, Vienna, 1826 and by Yechiel Halter, Warsaw, 1886.
translationCredits.canonicalSourceVersionTitle: Divrei Shalom v'Emet, tanslated by M. Bohnen, 2020
